newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK govt expects to auction more south island plots.
newsitem.headline: HK govt expects to auction more south island plots.

text.p: Hong Kong expects to auction three to four hectares of crown land for low-rise development on the south side of Hong Kong island in April to June, the first three months of next fiscal year, an official said on Wednesday.
Government land agent Francis Ng did not specify the type of land to be released, although sites in that district are usually slated for luxury residential development.
But Ng said the plan represented only a preliminary draft and the final auction schedule for the period would not be released until March.
"I hope in the first three months of next financial year, the government will be able to offer larger sites," he said, noting the two sites auctioned on Wednesday were not big.
A 2,008-square-metre site in Repulse Bay on the south side of Hong Kong island and a 5,080-square-metre site in Tuen Mun in the New Territories went under the hammer on Wednesday.
"In the next few months, I hope the government will be able to offer much larger sites for low-density or high-density development," he said.
He added that there were luxury residential sites all over the territory, not only on south side of Hong Kong Island.

Ng said there was no shortage of residential land supply and the territory expected to release 260 hectares of land for residential development over the coming five years, representing an average of 50 hectares every year.
"We are putting various categories of sites to meet various needs of the people, not just high-density or low-density, and all types of land," he said.
The land auction programme for the period from July 1997 to March 1998 will be released in July by the post-colonial government, Ng said.
Britain hands Hong Kong back to China at midnight on June 30.
